reports.title: Li Auto Inc. Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Business Outlook
section: For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects:
· | Deliveries of vehicles to be between 110,000 and 115,000 vehicles, representing a year-over-year increase of 0.7% to 5.3%.
· | Total revenues to be between RMB31.7 billion (US$4.7 billion) and RMB33.1 billion (US$4.9 billion), representing a year-over-year increase of 10.1% to 15.1%.
This business outlook reflects the Company’s current and preliminary views on its business situation and market conditions, which are subject to change.

desk.headline: Revenue up 5.4% to RMB28.8bn, beat; loss narrowed; Q4 outlook below consensus

other.label: Vehicle margin
other.change: vs 15.5% a year ago, 9.4% in Q2

other.label: Gross margin
other.change: vs 16.3% a year ago, 11.0% in Q2

other.label: Net loss (GAAP)
other.change: vs RMB624.4m loss a year ago

results: Revenue rose 5.4% to RMB28.8bn (US$4.3bn), above the RMB27.5bn estimate, on 7.2% more deliveries.
Gross margin recovered to 16.7% from 11.0% in Q2 on a richer model mix; vehicle margin was 15.3%.
The net loss halved to RMB309.7m; the adjusted loss per ADS was RMB0.12, much smaller than the RMB0.84 expected.
Operating cash flow was RMB3.2bn and free cash flow turned positive at RMB2.0bn; cash stood at RMB88.2bn.
Bought back US$169.7m of ADSs and HK$493.3m of shares in Q3; US$694.4m of the US$1.0bn programme is now used.

guidance.summary: For Q4 Li Auto expects 110,000–115,000 deliveries and revenue of RMB31.7–33.1bn (up 10–15% y/y), both below what analysts had expected.

points: Management expects gross margin to improve again in Q4, helped by cheaper lithium and in-house technology, and aims to return to profit.
CEO Xiang Li said the premium EV market (above RMB200,000) is flat this year, so carmakers are fighting over existing demand.
Li Auto is moving to a two-year model refresh cycle and plans one or two new standalone models in 2027.
Battery-electric models now make up more than half of deliveries; Li i6 capacity reached 20,000 a month in November.
Overseas sales are expected to double in 2027, with Li i6 deliveries in the Netherlands and Norway from Q1.
call.source: Call transcript — Investing.com, 25 Nov 2026; Q4 consensus from BigGo Finance, 25 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 deliveries reach the 110,000–115,000 range given the weaker-than-expected outlook.
Gross margin progress and whether the company does return to profit in Q4.
Early demand for the new Li i6, Li i9 and Li MEGA, and the European launch.
